lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: checking and interpreting

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: System: y = x + 2 and y = -x + 6. Does the point (1, 3) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?

steps: Check (1, 3) in the first equation: 1 + 2 = 3, which matches.
Check (1, 3) in the second equation: -1 + 6 = 5, which does not match 3.
The point satisfies the first equation but fails the second, so it fails the second equation only.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $22 flat fee plus $9 per month. Plan B charges a $24 flat fee plus $8 per month. The solution to the system is (2, 40). What does the y-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The difference in cost between the two plans.
The rate Plan B charges per month.
The number of months after which the two plans cost the same.
The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.

items.prompt: System: y = 4x - 17 and y = -x - 2. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?
Solve the system: y = 8x + 21 and y = -2x + 11. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
Relationship A: x: -5, -4, -3, -2 y: -5, -8, -11, -14. Relationship B: x: -5, -4, -3, -2 y: -19, -15, -11, -7. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: Solve the system: y = -2x + 14 and y = 3x + 14. In which quadrant does the intersection point lie, or does it lie on an axis?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
